procedure.method: Independent review in this current fresh session, with no spawning, forking or resuming. Verified all 13 explicitly supplied file pins by SHA-256 and byte count; read packet, case, rules, rubric, declared ratio policy and the two supplied manifests without following their unlisted embedded paths. Actually displayed A1/original.png first using tools.view_image(detail="original") and forwarded its returned image for visual inspection. Then displayed and inspected the three exact poster files in separate awaited view_image calls, in packet order: native, usage720, thumbnail320. All four successful displays preceded the first transcription judgment and any score. After complete viewing, recorded the first native copy reads and compared them by nfc-ws-optical-v1; no OCR, crops, edited views or ambiguity revisit were used. Read-only PNG header and blue-pixel extent measurements supplemented, but did not replace, the visual source comparison. No runtime thread ID is claimed; the runner owns provenance.

evidence.location: Central sculpture and both wall mounting points
evidence.observation: The complete cobalt-blue ribbon sculpture remains recognizable: a large tilted upper-left loop, a smaller lower-right loop, their central crossing, painted surface, two brass mounting points and soft wall shadows. Both outer loops are fully inside the poster; no added face or work tools are visible. The slight measured reduction is approximately uniform rather than a conspicuous aspect distortion.

evidence.location: Artwork position within the full native frame; top arch and lower-right loop
evidence.observation: Comparison with the actually viewed A1 source at the same 1122×1402 dimensions shows a small but consistent downward displacement and slight reduction of the artwork. Read-only blue-pixel extent measurement (B−R>25 and B−G>15, inclusive bounds; not complete-object segmentation) is source [123,239,976,1048] versus poster [127,274,968,1071]: the top is 35 px lower, the bottom 23 px lower, and the extent is 842×798 rather than 854×810. The blue extent center is 29 px lower (about 2.1% of frame height). The visible brass mounts likewise lie approximately at (252,342)/(891,747), versus (248,309)/(899,722) in A1. Identity, blue color and relative loop proportions survive, but the supplied photograph’s wall position is not maintained. This finding concerns the specified location, not pixel-for-pixel texture equality; it does not establish a redraw or a substituted artwork.

evidence.location: Upper title, central artwork and lower information block
evidence.observation: The supplied artwork is the main photographic subject; all six requested lines are visible. Date and address sit below the artwork without obscuring either loop. There are no extra copy lines, logos or sponsors.
One flat portrait poster retains a large blue artwork as a distinct nontext center; title and event information remain in separate wall areas.

issues: The explicit requirement to maintain the artwork’s wall position is not met: at unchanged native frame dimensions, the object is slightly smaller and displaced downward. The source and poster preserve the same recognizable artwork, not the same wall placement.

Date, address, explanatory sentence and URL remain readable against the pale wall; the shared left edge and single-line entries keep the copy organized.
The two smallest lines are much less comfortable to read at 256×320 than the title and date. They remain complete; this limits exceptional small-scale refinement rather than proving omitted glyphs.
